subfamily: whiskey Old-Fashioned with a split base (Codex p. 22: pull back the base, add a second spirit to accent it), ready-mixed with its water, freezer-cold, poured into a home-frozen ice shell and cracked at the table onto its own broken ice
glass: rocks glass (about 300 ml), holding a shell of ordinary cloudy ice frozen in a plastic cup
version: v3 (Tomás, round 6, final ruling): v1's numbers restored. Rye-led 3:1 split with Ron Zacapa 23 (recommended; Codex p. 109: this rum's affinity with rye, from its former whiskey barrels; the substitute style doesn't inherit the claim). Tied to Joly's 'Hugs, rum and rock' (Time Out Chicago 2014, F18). Water measured in (20 ml) in place of stirring. Freeform because no Arnold style models a ready-mixed drink poured over broken ice; judged by hand against his built range (27-32% / 6.5-8.5 g / 0-0.05%), plus melt cases after the crack. v2 (no rum: 60 rye / 12.5 syrup / 25 water, 31.0% / 7.88 g) also in range, kept on record.
